In this context, we examine the security risks associated with vertical and horizontal FL implementations. In order to prioritize data confidentiality, we develop a novel VHF algorithm, referred to as FedTAD, which effectively trains models for multi-party data scenarios involving both vertical and horizontal data partitions. We then conduct comprehensive evaluations of FedTAD utilizing real-world and artificially created datasets. Our findings demonstrate that the FedTAD model achieves comparable performance to centralized machine learning training, with improvements of up to 15% and 20% in the case of vertical and horizontal data divisions respectively, while significantly reducing communication costs. Additionally, our secure VHF framework was shown to be resilient to a range of attacks aimed at model inference. Our code has been made publicly available on GitHub at the following address: https://github.com/zhongjia-peng/FedTAD.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet their scalability to large datasets is severely limited due to the computationally expensive nature of pairwise evaluations. In response, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on larger data sets. While widely adopted, this method has significant drawbacks, notably requiring an unnecessarily large number of features, directly proportional to the size of the dataset, in order to achieve satisfactory results comparable to traditional kernel-based methods. In order to circumvent these limitations and efficiently process large datasets, this paper introduces an alternative method of kernel feature approximation, which we have termed the 'Compact Kernel Embedding' (CKE). CKE is based on a distinct analytical derivation of the RFF method and results in a significant improvement in both the number of features and center locations required to achieve performance comparable to the original kernel method. We demonstrate the improved performance and scalability of CKE in multiple machine learning applications.

In our study, we demonstrated how both a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner and a diagonal group are effectively incorporated into the wreath products under their combined, or product action, utilizing the Cartesian Decomposition technique.

This research paper examines conformally flat hypersurfaces of n-dimensional space (n is 4 or higher) within a hypersphere of n+2 dimensions. We start by classifying and describing these conformally flat hypersurfaces when they have constant M\"obius curvature under specific transformations. Next, we prove that a compact hypersurface with this constant M\"obius curvature, denoted R, is specifically equal to $(n-1)(n-2)r^2$ for values of r less than 1. Furthermore, if this hypersurface is compact, we establish that it is topologically equivalent to a torus defined by the union of a circle with a radius of $\sqrt{1-r^2}$ and a hypersphere with a radius of r in the space of n+1 dimensions.

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created to maximize energy gain and maintain a minimum data rate in a multi-user OFDMA network. Next, the model was refined to investigate throughput optimization in an SWIPT-enabled OFDMA system, resulting in a complex MINLP problem. Finally, an innovative Harvest-Then-Trellis technique was developed to support high-speed SWIPT applications.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers typically use percolation theory to study how network components become disconnected during attacks. In this study, we examine the effects of removing critical nodes in networks that cannot be disconnected by node removal, due to the presence of redundant paths. The focus is on small world networks, where the removal of nodes with the highest betweenness value can cause path failures, and where the percolation transition point remains unchanged despite changes in node removal methods. The rate at which percolation occurs after removing nodes with specific properties is explored and used to create simple differential equations to model this process. The solutions to these equations reveal the conditions under which complete percolation occurs in networks. The model is applicable to any network where there are no percolation transitions, making comparisons with random percolation possible. The approach also enables the comparison of network structures that resist percolation transitions. The method is applicable to network sizes that can be studied computationally, including small world networks of sizes up to 512 nodes.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss in optical recycling systems. Overcoming this constraint is crucial for identifying gravitational waves produced by binary neutron star mergers. We present a modified optical scheme, dubbed the Quantum Enhanced Sensitivity Setup, which boosts sensitivity above 700 Hz while maintaining the frequency range below which signal loss becomes significant. By leveraging the correlations inherent in quantum fluctuations, this design achieves a 2 decihertz improvement in strain noise floor at 1000 Hz and can detect the gravitational waves produced by neutron star neutron-rich fusion products in certain scenarios.

This research investigates the performance potential of extra-large scale MIMO systems with a high number of users, in scenarios with high user density in outdoor environments such as stadiums. A novel MIMO channel model is proposed that takes into account the spatial correlations and coupling among nearby users, allowing the analysis of a large-scale MIMO system with up to 256 antennas and an unlimited number of users in a stadium environment. The proposed model is shown to accurately represent the correlations, the effective noise, and the coupling among users, which are critical factors that affect the performance of large-scale MIMO systems. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that due to the increased correlations and the effective noise, the minimum eigenvalue and the capacity of a large-scale MIMO system decrease with an increase in the number of users. However, our findings also show that the optimal spacing between nearby users has a limited impact on the performance of a large-scale MIMO system in a stadium environment. Our research also explores the performance of various detection methods in a scenario with up to 256 antennas and an unlimited number of users. Our results demonstrate that the performance of detection methods improves with an increase in the spacing between the base and the users, but remains relatively stable with an increase in the number of users. Our research also presents simulation results that demonstrate the performance of a large-scale MIMO system in a real-world stadium environment based on real measurement data.

Recent observations near infrared and sub-millimeter wavelengths have revealed that the morphological structure of young stars' surrounding disks are complex, featuring various shapes such as symmetrical patterns, asymmetrical patterns, and partially destroyed shapes. Such diversity in structure can be attributed to the influence of gravitational forces from wide-orbit companions and, more significantly, objects in close-orbit that shape the disk into a particular form through ongoing accretion. When a close-orbit companion is present, material can be drawn from the disk to the companion through a process known as mass accretion, resulting in distinctive 'nose-shaped' features and vortex shapes within the disk. Aliphatic molecular hydrogen spectra can provide valuable insights into the conditions of the gas within these disks but are often difficult to obtain due to the high intensity of nearby emission from the central star. In such cases, the search can be made more effective by focusing on the weaker doublet component within the wider absorption feature, known as the Pa$\beta$.

A question remains about the secondary component in GW190814, as the observed characteristics of the neutron star or black hole are inconsistent with standard theories. Two possible interpretations have been proposed, either a transitional object between neutron stars and black holes with a large uncertainty of 0.12 $M_	ext{odot}$ or the accuracy of gravitational wave measurements being insufficient to confirm a special type of binary merger. A new analysis is presented that utilizes a neutron star equation of state indicator obtained from gravitational wave spectra, in the hope of shedding light on the truth about GW190814. Although the analysis fails to discern any distinguishing features from typical neutron stars or black holes in the GW190814 event, a novel finding shows that the estimated mass of the neutron star or black hole with the greater mass has a narrow range of 22.07 to 22.31 $M_	ext{odot}$ based on general relativity calculations. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the event could be associated with a massive neutron star in the range of 2.50 to 2.65 $M_	ext{odot}$, indicating that the parameter range remains viable until the GW190814 event analysis is significantly improved or the theory of general relativity is refined.

This research focuses on creating resilient Molmer-Sorensen gates using trapped ions arranged in a line, incorporating Gaussian amplitude modulation and a consistent laser frequency. We chose a frequency that maintains balanced entanglement accumulation across all motion modes to provide a significant degree of protection against frequency errors, particularly for long chains of ions. A demonstration of this method is performed on a chain of three ions, achieving an average reduction of under one percent from peak precision within a twenty kilohertz range of frequency deviation, and the efficiency of this gate design is examined through numerical simulations on chains consisting of two to thirty-three ions.

Lately, monolayer graphene on boron nitride has exhibited precise control over
electronic interactions due to its clean Dirac bands. However, this cleanliness
prevents the study of strong-hopping, umklapp processes essential for
interaction-induced physics. In this research, we engineered a twisted double
layer of graphene with a small twist angle (12.45 degrees) and a large interlayer
spacing (3.6 Angstrom). The resulting theoretical model shows that twisted
double layers can display a variety of features, including a large gap, a
van-Hove singularity, and a twisted tight-binding character. Most importantly,
the interlayer commensurability allows for strong umklapp processes in the
doped bands, offering a versatile laboratory to study strong interaction-induced
effects.

Researchers explored the capabilities of the NA62 experiment at CERN to enhance the restriction on the parameter |U_e|^2, which measures the coupling between electrons and heavy neutral leptons, to an unprecedented level of 2.7 ten-thousandth. This achievement is particularly significant when considering hidden-UV scenarios, where the heavy neutral lepton does not interact with quarks and charged leptons other than the electron. To reach this limit, the study analyzed various production pathways for the heavy neutral lepton and optimized the design of the NA62 detector to minimize neutrino background from the fixed target mode of operation. In doing so, the authors demonstrated that the na62 experiment can significantly expand the reach of existing constraints and provide a compelling motivation for further research at the NA62 facility.

Neural language models have largely surpassed $N$-gram models due to better performance, but our findings suggest that $n$-gram models still excel in many situations with low computational costs, demonstrating a strong foundation for our proposed extension. We've developed a new method called Neural-Augment, using neural models to refine models derived from $n$-gram training data, while maintaining efficiency. Our approach, which incorporates neural models in three different ways – blending, sequential training, and neural selector – successfully enhances models across various tasks and metrics when compared to standard techniques of continuing neural models, hybrid models, and neural-sparse methods. Our data and model augmentation framework has been made available online.

Reconstructing three-dimensional faces in complex real-world scenarios poses significant difficulties due to frequently missing or occluded facial details and the vast range of head positions and orientations present in these environments. As a result, developing effective methods for automating face alignment and reconstruction is crucial. Current automated approaches primarily rely on deep learning models that excel under ideal conditions but struggle with the kinds of challenges encountered in real-world settings. In contrast, automated methods based on convolutional human machine perception theories that incorporate prior knowledge about the subject have shown more promise. Building upon this concept, we propose an automatic framework called SADFA that leverages a combination of convolutional neural networks and geometric models to align and reconstruct three-dimensional faces. This approach enforces correct face alignment through an energy minimization technique that respects the inherent geometry of the face, allowing it to effectively handle challenging scenarios with freely posed and partially occluded faces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SADFA by achieving the highest accuracy on the challenging FP32 benchmark among all code-based submissions to the FacePG 2020 challenge.

In an inflationary model, with a specific type of $\alpha$-attractor potential, we examine the behavior in the high-$k$ regime, where cosmological perturbations exhibit excessive growth and negative values of the Bardeen potential. This regime facilitates the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). Our calculations demonstrate that a significant portion of dense primordial oscillations can be explained by the non-linear response of the $\alpha$-attractor model, particularly at high $k$ values. Furthermore, in this regime, where scalar fluctuations in the primordial gravitational waves' potential reside, we find that the corresponding scalar fluctuations can be over-dense and may form PBHs. Our findings suggest that a notable fraction of these PBHs could have masses within the range of $10^{-12}$ to $10^{-9}$ solar masses. This range aligns with that observed by the LIGO detector for binary black hole mergers. This prediction arises directly from the inflationary model, without requiring any additional assumptions.

Researchers examined marked ordered trees with the ability to designate some right edges as "optional", given they don't lead to leaf nodes. They employed this model to study skew Dyck paths. A key aspect studied was the number of deepest nodes in these marked trees. Through explicit generating functions, they obtained insights, revealing the average number of deepest nodes converges to $\frac53$ as the number of nodes increases, which can be contrasted to standard ordered trees with a convergent average of $2$ deepest nodes.

This investigation seeks to examine the capabilities of Informed OCR (iOCR) in accurately capturing vote tabulation data, as the system is designed with an advanced spell-checking feature to correct common errors associated with traditional OCR technology, which the research reveals results in iOCR outperforming traditional OCR methods.

In recent years, significant progress made by large-scale models and data applications underscores the relevance of investigating statistical estimation methods under non-ideal time series data conditions. This study examines a linear regression model featuring long-memory processes and time-varying coefficients, where we consider the impact of these processes on risk convergence rates in estimation and prediction tasks. Our main contribution involves establishing central limit theorems for the estimated parameters and establishing risk convergence rates under both independent and dependent data scenarios. Our research demonstrates the influence of long-memory processes and dependence on finite sample properties and estimation performance. A numerical example utilizing the Gaussian ARMA process is presented to complement our theoretical findings. This study's results can be applied to linear time series models featuring ARIMA processes.

A key factor for maintaining stability in future low-carbon power grids is expected to be energy storage systems. Studies examining past experiences reveal a common issue with storage units - they frequently fail to take advantage of high-price signals during periods of low energy supply. This behavior has been observed in both single-unit and aggregated models, despite their being designed to operate autonomously. In an effort to address this issue, this research develops a risk management approach for storage units, considering their individual reliability and willingness to engage in market uncertainty. Utilizing historical data from the Australian electricity market, storage units' behavior was found to be characterized by risk-averse tendencies in both individual and aggregated models. These models were then utilized to forecast future price patterns and probability distributions, resulting in improved risk management strategies for storage units. By engaging more freely with high-price signals and discounts during periods of low supply, these units can provide more valuable services to the grid, ultimately leading to a more stable and resilient power grid.

A computer model replicates the Earth's atmosphere on a sphere with a rotating, temperature-driven circulation, varying the rotation rate 3.5 to 10 times faster than the actual Earth's. Contrary to previous research, a recent study found that a rapidly rotating model resulted in one strong equatorial band of circulation, whereas slowing it down significantly increased circulation bands from one to six. For a model with an idealized solid surface, similar results held true even after introducing atmospheric instability and turbulence. Similar models were created with different atmospheric pressures and circulation patterns, but none showed the six-banded pattern observed in the slowed-down model. A similar six-banded pattern was observed in another model, one that included a solid surface and varied temperature, but it required a non-uniform surface temperature distribution. A related model that included a solid ocean's surface also demonstrated the six-banded pattern, but it required a specific range of surface temperature differences. A recent study suggested that the six-banded pattern might be linked to a specific Earth rotation rate that aligns with historical data, and could be caused by a change in circulation patterns influenced by a change in Earth's axis tilt.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) benefit from being trained on high-quality
dataset samples, but selecting these samples through active learning can
be time-consuming and costly. Our investigation combines active learning
with self-supervised pretraining, aiming to enhance DNNs efficiently.
Active learning is used to identify a small set of high-quality samples for
fine-tuning, while the majority of large-scale noisy data is used for
self-supervised pretraining. Our approach demonstrates substantial gains in
performance on three challenging classification tasks, with a significant
reduction in samples selected for fine-tuning. Our methods have been
extensively evaluated through ablation studies and a novel metric we call
the Active Learning Efficiency (ALE). Our findings show that our approach
enhances efficiency, supporting the importance of combining active learning
with self-supervised pretraining. Our code and models are available online at
the following repository: https://github.com/zhongjiehua/AdvActiveSelf.

Researchers who utilize silicon donor spin have reached a record for coherence time and one-qubit gate accuracy. To advance further, demonstrating the ability to execute reliable two-qubit logic operations with a strong coupling between qubits, specifically through exchange interaction, is crucial. To facilitate efficient development of large-scale quantum processors, a computational model of two-electron behavior has been created by applying a configuration interaction approach based on a multi-valley effective mass theory. By utilizing the code's efficiency to handle computational demands, exchange interaction effects, valley distribution, and electron distribution were examined in a range of positions, orientations, and under applied electric fields. The findings show that the exchange interaction can be managed by adjusting the position, orientation, and electric field but also indicates that the interaction's variability could pose a challenge for developing a universal quantum computer with silicon donors.

Our investigation focused on the transport properties of HgTe quantum wells near their critical thickness, where the energy gap is minimal, and the energy spectrum is described by a singular Dirac cone structure. Both large and small-sized (mesoscopic) samples made from the same material were examined as part of this study. When looking at small-sized samples, a well-defined, quantized resistance emerged in the absence of a magnetic field due to disorder effects. However, when a strong magnetic field was applied to larger samples, a unique pattern of resistance oscillations appeared in a wide range of field strengths, closely matching the field values identified in earlier optical studies. This matching was seen across multiple samples and was previously unknown in semiconductor research. All evidence suggests that the precise resistance resistance patterns are the direct result of interference between a wide range of helical edge states formed along the samples' length, and a sudden and sharp resistance drop occurred at a field strength where the edge states became in sync with each other, aligning with previous optical research.

In Dynamic Time-Division Duplexing (TDD), individual cells can schedule uplink and downlink modes independently, making it a key component for managing interference in cellular networks. However, identifying an optimal TDD configuration for a network of many cells is complicated due to varying channel conditions and available buffers in each cell, posing a significant challenge as it results in an NP-hard problem. Current solutions focus on local optimizations, neglecting the impact of interference between cells. We propose a novel distributed algorithm, called Distributed TDD Scheduling (DTS), which leverages the strengths and weaknesses of each cell through commodity market theory, ensuring that cells with more available buffer time are allocated for downlink transmissions, thus reducing interference. Furthermore, we prove that DTS results in stable equilibria, accurately models delay buffers and varies TDD configurations, and is asymptotically optimal compared to a hypothetical optimal solution. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of DTS through simulations based on real-world scenarios and data.

In this work, we introduce a novel meta-learning framework centered on ODE neural networks, which acquires an understanding of gradients. This framework grants optimizers enhanced flexibility and infuses an automatic inductive bias into tasks, as we have observed through testing on synthetic and real-world datasets in optimization tasks. Our current model outperforms a comparable baseline by $10x$ in the MNIST autoencoder meta-learning experiment and exhibits superior performance when applied to the Zeno scheme.

Simply enhancing a machine learning model's accuracy is not sufficient, as we must also focus on increasing its reliability. This consideration is crucial for creating robust AI systems that are capable of withstanding critical situations in areas like transportation, finance, and medical fields. We recommend developing a collaborative multi-agent framework that incorporates two trusted agents: one skilled in machine learning and a trustworthy reliability agent. This agent pair works together to improve both the model's precision and reliability through transfer learning, using neural networks. Our proposed method has several key benefits: it addresses uncertainty, leverages side information, and prevents overfitting. We tested this approach on multiple datasets and obtained results that demonstrate its superiority over existing techniques, winning first place in nine out of ten comparisons in a robust machine learning competition hosted on GitHub.

A newly defined polynomial, referred to as the nth toroidal colored Jones polynomial, is established for links in a thickened torus. Dubbed $J_n^T$, this polynomial demonstrates numerous properties similar to the original colored Jones polynomial, and notably displays volume conjecture behavior. By applying $J_n^T$, we prove the volume conjecture holds true for a specific link, the trefoil knot. Additionally, $J_n^T$ can be expressed through an algebraic construction utilizing quantum invariants from the around-the-monodromy algebra for the torus, which includes the Heisenberg algebra as a subset.

The primary objective of Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) involves
determining the appropriate sense of a word with multiple meanings in
a particular context.  Advances in deep learning, specifically the
use of LSTMs and attention mechanisms, have led to notable
improvements in automated WSD processes.  In response to the growing
need for scalable and efficient models for natural language processing
tasks, EfficientNet was recently introduced, incorporating a novel
subsampling-based architecture that achieves significant reductions in
model parameters while maintaining high performance.  Building upon the
success of EfficientNet, we introduce a new framework, SenseNet, which
effectively applies the principles of EfficientNet to accurately
resolve WSD tasks.  Through comparative experiments, we found that our
proposed SenseNet model delivers superior results, outperforming the
current state-of-the-art WSD models in multiple assessments.  To
further advance the field, we developed a Word Sense Induction dataset
called SENSEIND, which assesses a word's semantic similarity based on
context, in addition to releasing Word Sense Induction datasets for
individual word senses.

This study formulates a genuine integral expression of the reciprocal gamma function in terms of a modified hypersingular integral. It also proves the connection to the traditional complex representation, in addition to obtaining a modified complex representation following the standard Hankel path.

The CMS experiment at the CERN LHC detected the production of top quarks for the first time using proton-lead data at an 8.16 TeV nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy. Top quark production was identified in events featuring one isolated electron or muon and four or more jets, from a data set totaling 174 inverse nanobarns of luminosity. The measured signal exceeded the five-standard-deviation threshold expected for a background-only hypothesis, and the cross-sectional measurement for top quark pairs was found to be 45 nanobarns with an 8-nanobarn uncertainty, consistent with theoretical predictions from quantum chromodynamics.

This study focuses on key elements in cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing, specifically schema linking and value filling. To enhance encoding abilities, a column selection auxiliary task is proposed, leveraging explicit targets for relevance matching. Additionally, two value filling approaches are presented to bridge the gap between current zero-shot parsers and practical applications, considering that many existing parsers overlook value filling in synthesized SQL. Experiments on the Spider dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed approach over baseline models in terms of execution and exact set match accuracy when database contents are inaccessible, with further analysis pointing to areas for improvement.

This paper delves into the utilization of differential privacy within the framework of graph-based data. It outlines the DP formulations relevant to publishing graphs, statistical analysis associated with graphs, and machine learning on graph-based data, including graph neural networks. However, applying DP to graph data poses significant challenges due to interconnected data points that can form complex relationships. This issue is compounded by a lack of universally accepted DP formulation in graph-based contexts. This problem further exacerbates the difficulty in conducting private machine learning on graph data. A notable absence of systematised research on graph-based learning in relation to privacy was a key driver of our work, leading us to conduct various learning tasks on synthetic data using graph neural networks and SGC, before moving on to real-world data featuring Wikipedia link structures and Miami fruit fly gene expression networks. This investigation highlights several critical issues, including an inability to replicate secure graph learning results using existing methods, failing to achieve a 10% improvement in accuracy above the non-private baseline in multiple scenarios, and an analysis of optimisation challenges and potential improvements associated with private graph learning.

The vast amount of images, data, and resources that Euclid will generate positions the dataset as a significant legacy for astronomical communities. With an estimated 100 terabytes of data per year, the dataset will comprise high-quality images and spectroscopic information, significantly impacting the study of galaxies. Scientific findings expected from Euclid include precise observations of how galaxies have evolved and evolved at different distances, detailed information about the distribution of dark matter, insights into the nature of the universe's expansion and its rate of change, and an extensive collection of celestial objects in the solar system. To effectively manage and utilize this massive dataset, Euclid will employ advanced technologies, including a highly efficient data storage system and sophisticated instruments that minimize data generation. Furthermore, the project will provide extensive training and resources for researchers, offering them access to data, models, and tools, and facilitating collaboration and knowledge sharing among community members.

Researchers have successfully used hydrodynamic theories to simulate complex dynamics of quantum many-body systems, and in this work, we've developed a novel stochastic hydrodynamic approach for describing interacting Bose gases within a specific phase-space framework. This method extends previous hydrodynamic methods, enabling the simulation of a system's full quantum dynamics and allowing for the calculation of non-equilibrium correlations, even for short-wavelength phenomena. Building upon this description, we derived a linearized stochastic hydrodynamic model that simulates long-lasting non-equilibrium situations while maintaining the exclusion of forward scattering processes, and found it to be directly connected with the Luther-Emery liquid ladder architecture. Furthermore, we applied this model to study semi-thermal phase coherence in finite systems and predicted observable signatures in non-equilibrium correlations in cold atom experiments.

Given an independent and identically distributed sequence of letters broken down into words, an independent and identically distributed sequence of words broken down into letters is analyzed. An annealed large deviation principle (LDP) for the empirical process of words is established, with the rate function derived as the average specific relative entropy relative to a reference ensemble of words, conditioned on the empirical letter frequency of the underlying sequence. This result applies to both Markovian and non-Markovian contexts. A related goal is the proof of a non-annealed LDP for the latter cases, which is a more challenging and open issue. This research builds upon previous studies by [Derrida and Elisabeth (2003), Ruelle (2009)], and new examples and references are provided.

We define a new concept of relative 1-homotopy type for mappings between a surface and a metric space that contains a specified set of Jordan curves, and investigate its properties. This enables us to prove the existence and local smoothness of the surfaces with minimal area within a particular relative 1-homotopy class, following a previous work by the second author. Furthermore, we establish an isoperimetric inequality for surfaces with minimal area, bounded by Jordan curves with a specific property, and this result leads to a third proof of the existence of a surface with minimal area and a specific boundary condition.

Recent studies on the 64Ni nucleus with a low-spin structure have provided significant insights, revealing multiple 0+ and 2+ excited states below 4.5 MeV and confirming the previously observed 4+ and 6+ levels at 2799 keV and 3799 keV respectively. Using a combined approach of differential elastic scattering, inelastic scattering, and particle identification, researchers have effectively clarified the 64Ni nucleus' low-spin structure. This understanding was made possible through a series of experiments at the RIBF Radioactive Ion Beam Factory in Japan using the RIPS and RIBT separators and the Super Water Chunnel (SWC) recoil separator and detector, in collaboration with the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) and the Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research in Germany. A structural transition was observed in the pre- and post-neutron 64Ni nuclei, facilitating a deeper comprehension of this transition and the spin-zero ground state of the 63Ni nucleus, which served as a source for neutrons in these experiments.

Machine learning models often undergo performance assessment through k-fold cross-validation to facilitate model selection and parameter adjustment. Yet, due to the random partitioning inherent in CV, estimated performance metrics exhibit significant variability. This unpredictability makes effective parameter tuning challenging, as it introduces substantial uncertainty into model selection. To address this issue, this research paper proposes an alternative approach, dubbed the Expected Optimistic Model Selection (EOMS), which accounts for performance metric estimation error and avoids unnecessary model evaluations. By analyzing model performance estimation error and incorporating an expectation of the optimal performance, EOMS method reduces the number of model evaluations required and brings the selected model closer to the true optimal model. Experimental results demonstrate that EOMS significantly outperforms traditional approaches in both real-world datasets and benchmark datasets.

Deep Neural Networks with vast parameters have faced challenges in real-time deployment, prompting the use of Teacher-Student architectures. In these systems, a smaller student network learns from a pre-trained teacher model, reducing computational requirements while maintaining performance. The student and teacher models are often trained simultaneously to achieve high accuracy, with key applications including knowledge distillation for data compression and multi-task learning. Recent research has leveraged attention mechanisms and feedback loops to enhance results, but is generally focused on single-task training. Here, we explore the use of Teacher-Student architectures in a more complex multi-task learning setting, incorporating three challenging computer vision tasks: object classification, segmentation, and detection. To overcome difficulties with shared resources and task-specific information, an attention-based feedback loop was implemented, demonstrating the potential of this technique to be scalable and adaptable for a wide range of tasks and datasets. Experimental results indicate significant improvements over conventional methods, with performance on the ADE20K and PASCAL VOC12 datasets beating the original scores by 8.2% and 4.8% respectively, and the MS COCO dataset by 6.8% when compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a new efficient framework for representing functions in graphical models, which serves as a foundation for a variety of computational tasks. Our concise model then leverages this framework, specifically using deterministic finite state automata within a variable elimination approach known as Bucket Elimination. We dub this variant FABE, which we found significantly enhances Bucket Elimination by substantially reducing the computational time and memory usage. Our FABE approach compares favourably to the current state of the art methods, particularly recursive best-first and structured message passing for the most probable explanation, as well as CPLEX, GUROBI and toulbar2 for constrained optimisation, by achieving a 5 orders of magnitude reduction in computational time and a 10,000 fold memory reduction in a representative set of complex scenarios.

We investigated the absorption of a single, monochromatic light beam at 689 nm as it passes through a cloud of ultracold $^{88}$Sr atoms. Due to the interaction, the absorption pattern deviates significantly, taking on an asymmetric shape as a result of a shift in frequency that is equivalent in magnitude to the natural width of a specific atomic transition in strontium. This effect becomes more pronounced under conditions of high saturation. Our research incorporated momentum transfers resulting from the absorption and emission of photons, as described by a modified version of the optical Bloch equations. We demonstrated that even a single-beam setup can demonstrate Ramsey interference patterns, eliminating the need for coherent population trapping, through proper manipulation of the light intensity and duration.

When subjected to high stresses, the vast majority of dense mixtures undergo a sudden and extreme thickening, characterized by a transition from fluid-like behavior to rigidity. Researchers propose that interactions between elongated particles that link to the surrounding fluid, in contrast to colliding particles with non-hydrodynamic interactions, drive this transition. They demonstrate through numerical simulations that, as shear stress increases, suspensions made of prolate particles shift from hard-sphere-like behavior, and demonstrate that this phenomenon occurs regardless of the particles' aspect ratio. Furthermore, they show that the stress required for the transition to happen is inversely related to the particles' eccentricity, and that the resulting rigid structure has a similar microstructure, regardless of the particles' shape. This is especially evident when comparing to actual data from an experimental system, a highly eccentric particle system.

Recently, the centralizer of a diagonal embedding of U(sl2) within the U(gl4) algebra was discovered, revealing the special Racah algebra as a subalgebra of U(gl4). A preceding study established the basis transformation rules for the special Racah algebra utilizing the 6j symbols from U(gl4), but it did so relative to the basis of U(gl4). In this study, the basis transformation rules were re-expressed in an absolute basis of the special Racah algebra, leading to both absolute and relative versions of the Fock-Bargmann transform annotated with 9j and 6j symbols respectively. Furthermore, absolute and relative versions of the discriminant algebra under the same Diagonal Unitary Group were also derived and found to be isomorphic to the special Racah algebra.

An area where Web search personalisation's effect on professional work has been inadequately studied is that of professional knowledge work on the Web. This study examines how search engine optimisation (SEO) influences knowledge work by combining an in-depth analysis of 18 semi-structured interviews with Web developers and a large-scale Web scraper of 329 SEO-related Web pages. Our findings reveal that SEO can significantly limit access to essential information for Web developers and suggest that up to 75% of necessary information may be unreachable due to personalisation and algorithmic search results. Furthermore, our research reveals that certain search engine features, such as 'news,' can help Web developers discover relevant information, although these features are not commonly used. Our data also indicate that Web developers rely heavily on the Internet's top 5 search engines for all information, including both professional and non-professional in nature. Finally, our research demonstrates that Web developers' perceptions of search engine personalisation are either under- or overestimates of its actual impact on their work.

We are proposing the construction of a state-of-the-art muon-proton and muon-nucleus collider, which could be built either alone or as part of a future complex of colliders in Dongchuan, Yunnan, China. This proposed collider would allow for groundbreaking research in nuclear and particle physics disciplines such as hadron physics, precision physics, and beyond-standard-model physics. By operating at multiple energy levels, it can achieve unprecedented levels of precision in precision physics and provide comprehensive data in hadron physics research. With design capabilities for an annual luminosity of 1.5 x 10 to the power 32, it can yield a wealth of data in hadron physics and precision physics at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Kunming Nuclear Physics Institute.

A novel approach is proposed to create a respiratory motion compensation technique via MRI, designed to produce high-quality images while minimizing artifacts caused by breathing movements. A fast, free-breathing T2-weighted MRI sequence was developed and improved to provide consistent, motion-free images for building an atlas, then used with a computational model to generate four different respiratory states and create a 4D atlas. This atlas model was used to compensate for respiratory motion in MRI images acquired under controlled breathing, modeled as an intermediate state. The comparison showed that the control breathing atlas registration produced higher Dice similarity coefficients (average 0.951) in registered images than the free-breathing atlas registration (average 0.901). Moreover, the control breathing atlas registration produced lower surface overlap metrics (average 0.956) compared to the free-breathing atlas registration (average 0.918). The registration to the atlas created from the mid-expiration MRI scans showed higher surface overlap metrics (average 0.949) in comparison to the registration to the atlas created from the free-breathing MRI scans (average 0.918). The proposed method was found effective in compensating for respiratory motion caused artifacts in MRI scans acquired under free breathing conditions, also providing a suitable template for reconstructing 4D anatomy from two 1.5 T MRI scans acquired under controlled breathing, modeled as an intermediate state of the respiratory cycle.

The paired-permutation test in NLP systems has long relied on testing the statistical significance of differences in performance. This test aims to verify that observed discrepancies aren't simply coincidental. Despite the importance of accurate results, a lack of suitable exact algorithms forces practitioners to use time-consuming Monte Carlo approximations to achieve this goal. In contrast, we've developed an efficient method for calculating paired-permutation test results exactly. This exact algorithm takes significantly less time to compute than Monte Carlo methods. In particular, we observed a 10 times speedup when using our exact algorithm versus the commonly employed Monte Carlo approximation on a representative dataset of 20000 samples.

A comprehensive dataset of freight rates, shipping quantities, new ship prices, used ship prices, and scrapped ship prices has been assembled from 1966 to 2009 for the six primary shipping routes. Furthermore, instructions on combining and verifying datasets using the knowledge of shipping industry experts and former top management members are provided. A descriptive analysis of previously unstudied market phenomena known as the "container crisis" is conducted with this data. Structural changes in the data variables are then identified to demonstrate how the dissolution of shipping monopolies affected market behavior.

We define loom spaces as a more general framework incorporating leaf spaces for pseudo-Anosov flows and link spaces for veering triangulations. Building on Gu\'eritaud's research, it is demonstrated that there is a veering triangulation inherently linked to every loom space, with this triangulation's realization being topologically equivalent to 3D space.

The recent surge in financial media information, fueled by rising
online sources, has made it essential to examine the impact of
news headlines and sentiment on the stock market using machine learning.
Our research utilizes a vast dataset of daily news articles and
corresponding stock price movements for 12 major technology companies,
processing it to create a dataset with high dimensions. We developed two
models, one using multi-task wide learning and the other graph-based
methods, to analyze the complex relationships between the text features,
stock price movements, and a sentiment index. Our results show that both
approaches effectively incorporate the external information, resulting in
accurate predictions of stock price movements and a reliable sentiment
index. We processed the models' outputs to create a simplified framework
for guiding investors, and our research also compares different machine
learning techniques for better performance.

This research investigates the double Higgs boson production at future electron-positron colliders CLIC and ILC with TeV-scale energies within the framework of Effective Field Theories (EFTs), focusing on Beyond Standard Model Higgs physics. Initially, we consider the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) and then compare the predictions with the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Our primary concern is effective theories that extend the Standard Model up to a very high scale, where we examine the capabilities of future double Higgs boson production measurements at these colliders. We develop an analytical formula for the double Higgs boson production cross-section at the electron-positron colliders CLIC and ILC, incorporating the impact of polarization effects within the HEFT/SMEFT framework. We also determine the sensitivity of these colliders to the effective operators Proportionality $|{\cal C}_3^2+{\cal C}_4^2|$ or ${\cal C}_5^2$, which corresponds to $1.5-6.9$ times the compositeness scale $f$, depending on the collider and the effective operator. We find that at the 300 GeV center-of-mass energy CLIC, the effective operator Proportionality $|{\cal C}_3^2+{\cal C}_4^2|$ or ${\cal C}_5^2$ can be detected at the level of $2.5$ times

We perform a covariant expansion of the Einstein-Hilbert action in powers of
$1/c^2$, considering a generic spacetime foliation defined by $c$, the speed
of light. We achieve this through the application of a suitable 'pre-non-
relativistic' geometrical parametrization, thereby facilitating an
analytical $1/c^2$ expansion of general relativity. Ultimately, this method
permits an in-depth examination of the Einstein-Hilbert action expansion up to
its next-to-next-to-leading order.

The movement of long, thin objects moving through granular materials has been studied by analyzing the drag they experience and how it changes direction in relation to their movement. Using high-speed cameras and particle image velocimetry, researchers observed a significant increase in drag experienced by a cylindrical object with its long axis perpendicular to its direction of movement, especially in low confinement, where the ratio of the object's length to its diameter is greater than 10. A dimensionless parameter was used to analyze and compare the results in different confinement conditions, showing that the drag experienced by the object is much greater when its long axis is perpendicular to its movement, especially in low confinement, where the difference is about 10 times greater than in high confinement. A model that takes into account the disorder of the granular material was used to explain the results, showing that the drag experienced by the object is much greater when its long axis is perpendicular to its movement due to the formation of voids on the sides, which increase the drag in this orientation.

Our research examined the connection between initial anisotropic geometry and anisotropic flow within a multiphase transport model, specifically for 200 GeV Au+Au and Cu+Cu collisions. Contrary to elliptical flow, triangular flow doesn't demonstrate a clear rise with increasing centrality. Instead, it appears to decrease or remain steady across various collision scenarios. We also discovered that initial tri-axial correlations, influenced by long-range tri-plateau fluctuations, contribute significantly to final triangular distributions. Furthermore, our analysis revealed that shorter-range tri-axial correlations, resulting from hydrodynamic reactions, also impact initial conditions and, in turn, affect triangular flow.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has achieved precise measurements in two areas, namely neutral B meson mixing and CP violation, as well as in rare electroweak processes occurring in suppressed B-meson decays. This study concentrates on recent findings from the ATLAS collaboration, encompassing evaluations of rare occurrences like $B^0_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+\mu^-$ decays and the determination of CP-violating processes in $B^0_s \to J/\psi\phi$.

This article examines the fundamental requirements for numerical methods solving
time-dependent partial differential equations, with a focus on preserving the
initial conditions and maintaining long-term stability in the presence of
dissipation and forcing. A general framework for developing and evaluating
numerical schemes is presented, using the one-dimensional heat equation as an
example. Within this framework, the algorithm is applied to solve an altered
version of the equation, adding a source term and specifying the solution's
final state. To ensure that the scheme preserves the initial conditions and the
final state, conditions are established and numerically verified through
computations.

Soft-tissue navigation is highly dependent on non-rigid registration. For laparoscopic liver surgery, we developed an automatic method that uses a sparse set of landmark-tracking data to register a pre-surgical MRI model with a dynamic liver surface. This approach assumes limited access to tracking data, making it suitable for mini-laparoscopic liver surgery. We evaluated this method using phantom and ex-vivo porcine data, comparing the registered models to ground truth through a distance metric and surface deviation analysis. Furthermore, we applied this method to data from two human subjects, demonstrating its practicality in a clinical setting.

Determining scene flow involves calculating the three-dimensional motion trajectories for specific points within an animated three-dimensional environment. Motion trajectory data can be beneficial for various tasks, such as classifying moving objects, identifying moving objects, and creating realistic animations. However, calculating accurate scene flow remains a complex and time-consuming task due to the need to analyze multiple images and three-dimensional models. In response, deep learning techniques have led to the development of efficient methods for estimating scene flow from single images or pairs of images using neural networks. In the context of multi-view scene flow estimation, most current approaches rely on point cloud data or 3D models with surface normals, neglecting important information present in binary edge maps. In this paper, a novel method called SFD-Net is introduced, which utilizes input data featuring edge maps and two images to estimate multi-view scene flow. The proposed technique leverages two separate networks to compute motion vectors from edge maps and images, resulting in a solution for single-view vector estimation. The derived vectors are then projected onto a three-dimensional space to obtain precise point cloud data, enabling the use of common metric learning techniques to calculate global shapes without requiring explicit 3D models. The proposed approach demonstrates superior performance in comparison to existing methods according to metrics evaluated on public datasets.

In recent years, AI networks, specifically those based on artificial neural systems, have significantly outperformed competitors in a wide range of tasks including image recognition, sound analysis, and language interpretation. However, widespread use of such models was previously hindered due to their massive computational requirements. Neuromorphic computing technology, which allows bio-realistic neural networks to operate at high speeds while minimizing energy consumption, has now become an appealing substitute. In order to effectively train and test neural networks on this hardware, new algorithms are required. This paper presents a novel method for training and testing SNNs in a way that is compatible with INP-based hardware, incorporating a spiking reservoir to significantly enhance model performance and enable efficient computation. Experimental results show that using this approach, SNNs are able to achieve notable improvements (over 10%) in accuracy in challenging MNIST and Receptive Field Translation tasks with only a small increase in the number of parameters (less than 5%).

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. We derived the free energy of spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of a strong magnetic field and temperature, and subsequently determined its key thermodynamic properties such as the pressure, energy density, entropy density, and heat capacity of spin-polarized strange quark matter. Our study reveals that when the temperature decreases and the ratio of the temperature to the mass of light quarks is less than one, the heat capacity of spin-polarized strange quark matter increases with temperature. Additionally, when the ratio of the temperature to the mass of light quarks is less than one, the entropy density and heat capacity of spin-polarized strange quark matter approach a linear relationship with temperature.

A Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property in graph theory refers to the characteristic where a graph has matching subgraphs, each corresponding to an edge, connecting all vertices in a specific order. This property can be identified by tracing paths between the centers of matchings in a graph with even degree vertices. A subgraph is considered a center of a matching if no edge connects two of its vertices, and all edges connect a vertex to a vertex outside of it. A new algorithm has been developed to automatically recognize the Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property in graphs by employing a method based on the graph's symmetries, eliminating the need for manual tracing. This algorithmic approach is demonstrated through the analysis of a nontrivial example - a graph with the PMH-property, consisting of multiple petals, each with an symmetrical loop, as revealed by graph symmetry analysis.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call filtering policies in containerized applications. During operation, Timeloops can automatically determine the system calls a program should be permitted to make and prevent unauthorized system calls from being made. In addition, Timeloops rectifies various shortcomings of static analysis-based techniques, such as the creation of highly precise filters for programs in languages like JavaScript and PHP. Developed using standard, reliable technologies, Timeloops features a simple and efficient design comprising less than 500 lines of code. Our research demonstrates that a kernel-based approach like Timeloops is capable of generating system call filters with precision exceeding 99.9% for various applications, while causing minimal performance slowdown.

This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target appearance probabilities are organized on a grid. A streamlined variation of the Rao-Blackwellized point mass filter predicts the density of unobserved targets, with their distribution approximated as Gaussian for locally unobserved targets. The research team also designs an algorithm to update grid-based target appearances and estimates uncertainty in target densities as Gaussian mixtures. In contrast to conventional Gaussian mixture models, this approach reduces data storage and computation by limiting the number of target appearances within predetermined grid cells. As a result, this method is particularly suited for high-dimensional state spaces with limited field of regard, such as in sensor management applications. In these scenarios, the method excels at managing the trade-off between target density estimation and sensor usage by prioritizing areas with higher target appearance probabilities and greater uncertainty.

This study examines the null controllability of a population model that includes an interior degenerate diffusion component. By first establishing a new Carleman estimate for the adjoint system in its entirety, and subsequently deriving a relevant observability inequality, we aim to demonstrate the existence of a localized control action capable of driving the population towards extinction within a finite time frame.

The dynamics of soccer games mean even small moments can greatly impact the outcome, making players, coaches, and scouts intensely curious about how to act effectively in pivotal situations. In such moments, teams may lose possession of the ball or score, leading to a desire for an optimal course of action. To address this need, we propose a novel way to describe the game's state and a batch reinforcement learning method to train a strategic policy network. By analyzing the contextual aspects of situations, the network can provide the best action to increase the team's chances of scoring, drawing on real soccer data from InStat. In a large-scale experiment with 104 European soccer matches, we found that an expert policy could significantly improve on amateur players' decisions, even after accounting for the players' skill level. Furthermore, we discovered that situations with similar descriptions shared a common reward function, enabling us to train a general policy without access to loss-of-score data. Our approach and findings offer a groundwork for future research in soccer strategy and decision-making.

High-resolution subsurface modeling via seismic imaging has the potential to be greatly improved with Full Waveform Inversion (FWI).  However, FWI's limited convergence and susceptibility to local minima hold it back from achieving this goal.  An alternative method, Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (WRI), was recently proposed as a more stable and convergent alternative.  In (WRI), the model is represented as an impedance matrix, and the data misfit is defined in the frequency domain using wavefields, with no need to match recorded data exactly.  An important aspect of (WRI) is the need to solve the wave equation for forward modeling, which can be computationally expensive.  To address this, this work leverages an approximate linearized forward operator from Full Waveform Inversion, replacing the exact solution with an attenuated source wavefield.  Attenuated Source Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (ASWRI) adds source attenuation to the (WRI) method, which helps prevent blowup of the data misfit.  To solve the non-linear problem, an iterative strategy is employed, coupling with a linearized solver using an Algebraic Multi-level Fast Waveform Transformation (AM-FWT) method for acceleration.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetric binary fusion process model was developed for endponts in a flow network. The model determines the outcome of species competition at each network endpoint and the species that inhabits each endpoint as a result of random events and connections to neighboring endpoints. It was found that the species competing for network endpoints share many characteristics, including being markovian, having paths of descending lengths where species competition ends, and accurately being simulated by Monte Carlo methods. Additionally, it was discovered that the species that inhabits each endpoint is independently decided by a process that is independent of the network, which allows for the examination of species competition against a neutral background.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. This hybrid network allows a central hub to transfer data to those in need and supplies power to devices in energy deficit. This coexistence enables the hub to serve a group of energy-abundant users who act as a relay for those in energy deficit. A problem-solving method is proposed to maximize energy and achieve a high data transfer rate. The goal is two-fold: (1) determine the energy transfer policy and optimize power and data transfer rates, (2) calculate the optimal power and area for an integrated network. This method uses an intelligent reflecting surface and D2D communication. The problem is then defined as maximizing the minimum rate under a rate limit constraint in D2D communication and an energy transfer constraint at the hub. This is formulated as a mixed-integer optimization problem. Due to its complexity, this problem is then transformed into Geometric Program form to achieve a feasible solution. This solution is then proven to satisfy D2D communication constraints. Finally, an algorithm is proposed to calculate the optimal power and area for an integrated network. This algorithm is tested under various conditions to provide simulation results. This shows that an increased energy transfer budget leads to a higher data transfer rate. The surge in telework needs has highlighted the potential benefits of
automating and controlling experiments remotely. This work presents the technical
advancements of creating a two-dimensional LDV measurement system using a single-
point LDV system via a remotely controllable and automated setup. The document's
aim is to expedite the development of similar setups for this kind of application,
which is highly versatile and can be applied to various scenarios including both
air-based acoustic signal-driven samples and mechanically induced samples.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is subject to debate 
due to varying design parameters. Our study delves into the capabilities of these 
phase plates, particularly in relation to spherical aberration correction in 
Transmission Electron Microscopes. We determined the possible resolutions, 
ranging from 0.8 to 3.6 Angstroms, achievable with these phase plates in three 
specific configurations. These results demonstrate that phase plates can be 
optimized for a wide range of applications, including imaging tiny lattice 
structures and macroscopic thin films. We also calculated the optimal focus 
ranges and corresponding resolutions for each design. Furthermore, we analyzed 
the influence of focus on imaging quality and examined the unique features 
observable in aberration-corrected images, particularly in the presence of 
negative spherical aberration. We conclude by discussing the potential benefits 
and limitations of employing phase plates with predefined aberrations.

This study examines the spectral properties of solitary wave solutions for a nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with nonlocal feedback. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of a solitary wave solution and its variational characterization. Furthermore, we establish the boundaries in the complex plane where the linearized operators lack real spectrum, revealing that the combination of the delay and the nonlocal feedback extends the spectrum's stability region compared to the classical case. We also observe that the variation of the potential energy can be related to the linearized operator's index, which, together with the delay and nonlocality properties, enables us to apply the Conley-McKenna's criterion for spectral stability. We demonstrate that under certain conditions, the solution's stability is achieved, even when the potential energy's variation has a positive index. We also investigate the properties of the linearized operator and its symbol, which enable us to apply the Nirenberg-Wirginer-Taylor reduction and further analyze the (1+1)-dimensional case. For this dimension, we find that the solution's stability is achieved when the potential energy's variation has an index greater than zero. We also derive an explicit formula to determine the solution's stability in the (1+1)-dimensional case.

We derive new conclusions regarding the additive Galois module properties of specific wildly ramified finite non-abelian extensions of Q. Notably, in cases where a Galois extension with a A4, S4, or A5 Galois group is given, we determine essential and sufficient freedom requirements for the ring of integers within its associated quadratic field extension. Additionally, these results can be applied to demonstrate the freeness of a specific, infinitely generated group over a rational group algebra, which can be considered a precursor to deeper research on the associated problems of integral Galois module structure and non-abelian reciprocity laws.

In experiments involving particle collisions, identifying neutral long-lived particles relies on either finding decay products at unusual locations or missing energy. While both methods are effective, missing energy is more sensitive, especially with higher luminosity. This study examines the effectiveness of this approach for detecting axion-like particles at the Belle II experiment, which has the capability to detect such particles with masses between 0.4 and 10 GeV using the $B^+ \to K^+ E_i$ decay channel at rates exceeding 10. It is also possible to modify the Belle II detector to increase this sensitivity to masses beyond 10 GeV. This research demonstrates that the Belle II experiment can detect neutral long-lived particles at rates exceeding 5 at the LHCb experiment's sensitivity levels, which are achievable using optimized missing energy searches involving the $B_s^0 \to J/\psi E_i$ and $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^- E_i$ decay channels for masses and branching ratios that are currently beyond reach.

This study examines the potential shortcomings of contextualized embedding-based techniques, popular in natural language processing, particularly for identifying historical changes in word meanings over time. Despite their effectiveness in other tasks, our research reveals that these methods may struggle with a significant aspect of diachronic analysis and highlights key issues with current approaches using contextualized embeddings in this context. Our findings demonstrate that models capable of accounting for contextual dependencies may not adequately capture subtle temporal developments in word meanings and highlight the importance of pretraining models on historical text corpora for accurate detection of temporal semantic evolution. We also introduce a new contextualized embedding-based method, Contextualized Diachronic Semantic Change Analysis (CDSCA), which utilizes a combination of both static and contextualized embeddings to accurately identify and quantify historical changes in word meanings and avoids the limitations of single contextualized embedding-based methods. Our experiments using historical American and British English texts demonstrate that CDSCA outperforms existing methods based on contextualized embeddings in both corpora. Furthermore, our analysis shows that pretrained models trained on historical texts can effectively capture temporal developments in word meanings and that CDSCA can be applied to a wide range of diachronic text analysis tasks.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) contain accreting material around a supermassive black hole and allow the investigation of black hole mass and spin through the analysis of electromagnetic spectra. This study classifies various methods used to determine the parameters of AGNs based on their luminosity properties. It examines the relationships between bolometric luminosity and the mass and spin of the black hole, as well as how these relationships can be applied to different AGN types. It also looks at the limitations of the methodological framework, including the assumptions made in modeling the jets of radiating matter and the variability of the method due to the behavior of the AGN. It further explores the application of the method to individual AGNs and surveys, considering factors like the accuracy of the photometric measurements and the effects of the environment on the variability of the method. It also discusses the potential for direct mass measurement through test masses in gravity sensors based on the application of the technique to the event horizon of Sagittarius A*, and it highlights the potential for indirect mass measurement based on the analysis of extreme random fluctuations based on the application to the event horizon of Sgr A*.
